content: Twenty years from now you will be more disappointed by the things that you didn't do than by the ones you did do.
author: Mark Twain
story:
Preserved as part of Mark Twain's enduring intellectual legacy, this reflection addresses the fundamental nature of regret and happiness. Across his life and work, Mark Twain returned repeatedly to the conviction that personal integrity, honest observation, and clarity of purpose are the foundational pillars of a life well-lived.

Contemplating this truth invites us to step back from the frantic rush of daily demands. By examining our assumptions with fresh eyes, we discover the inner grounding necessary to act with wisdom and quiet conviction.
